recent_posts.title: How Deutsche Telekom degrades 20% of the internet for German fiber customers
recent_posts.summary: Deutsche Telekom (AS3320) refuses to peer directly with Cloudflare at DE-CIX Frankfurt, forcing traffic through congested transit providers like GTT. This causes latency spikes from 10ms to 180ms+ during peak hours, degrading roughly 20% of the internet for German fiber customers paying €70/month for 1 Gbit/s service. Telekom, a privatized monopoly built on taxpayer-funded infrastructure, demands above-market peering fees from content providers — a practice consumer advocates call 'double paid traffic.' Vodafone has now followed suit by withdrawing from public internet exchanges. A coalition including Epicenter.works and Stanford professor Barbara van Schewick filed a formal complaint with Germany's Bundesnetzagentur. Workarounds include switching ISPs, routing Cloudflare traffic via a VPS with better Telekom connectivity using Tailscale, or using mtr/traceroute to document issues for regulatory complaints.

recent_posts.title: Using One OAuth App for Multiple Virtual Hosts with Caddy Security
recent_posts.summary: OAuth apps require exact callback URL matches, making multi-host setups tricky. Caddy Security's redirect_url parameter solves this by centralizing the OAuth flow on a single auth domain, then redirecting users back to their originating virtual host. The approach requires one authorization policy per virtual host, each specifying its own redirect_url pointing back to the respective app domain.

recent_posts.title: Automatic WireGuard Failover with NixOS and Prometheus
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building automatic WireGuard VPN failover on NixOS using systemd services and Prometheus metrics. The solution uses three components: wg-select for initial server selection on boot, wg-failover for switching to the healthiest server, and wg-health-check for continuous monitoring. Two smokeping probers provide health data — one external (on the hypervisor) measuring reachability to all VPN endpoints, and one internal (inside the VPN namespace) measuring actual tunnel quality. The health check runs every minute and triggers failover after three consecutive checks showing over 15% packet loss, with Prometheus serving as the authoritative source of server health data.

recent_posts.title: Bypassing Telekom's Cloudflare Congestion with Tailscale
recent_posts.summary: A practical workaround for Telekom's congested Cloudflare peering using Tailscale subnet routing. By advertising Cloudflare's IP ranges through a €1/month IONOS VPS (which has direct peering with Cloudflare at BCIX Berlin), connection times dropped from 11+ seconds to under 400ms. The setup uses NixOS on both the home router and VPS, with Tailscale handling route advertisement and NAT automatically. Caveats include ~5ms added latency, ~500 Mbps VPS bandwidth cap, and the VPS becoming a single point of failure for Cloudflare access.

recent_posts.title: Why do agents always speak text?
recent_posts.summary: When an LLM agent calls a tool like kubectl, data that starts as ~4KB of protobuf ends up as ~12K tokens in the model's context due to text serialization. The root cause is that agent-tool wire protocols are string-typed, and models have no learned representation for binary formats. The practical workaround is piping output through tools like jq to reduce token count. The author argues a typed binary channel between tools and models would address the problem at the source, potentially starting with data-analysis agents using Apache Arrow, but notes the pressure to build it is low because the jq workaround is good enough.

recent_posts.title: Auto-updating ESPHome Devices with Home Assistant
recent_posts.summary: A short guide showing how to automate ESPHome firmware updates across multiple devices using a Home Assistant automation. The provided YAML automation runs nightly at 3:15am, finds all ESPHome devices with pending updates, and installs them automatically via the update service. The author notes this approach is reliable as long as you avoid low-level Lambda functions in your ESPHome configs.

recent_posts.title: Running iBGP Over WireGuard for DN42 and Beyond
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of setting up iBGP over a dedicated WireGuard tunnel to propagate DN42 routes from a VPS to a home network. The post explains why Tailscale fails for this use case (it only forwards explicitly advertised subnets), then details the WireGuard /30 tunnel configuration with allowedIPsAsRoutes=false, Bird routing daemon config for both home router and VPS route reflector, firewall rules, and IPv6 next-hop handling. The result is automatic route propagation for both DN42 and arbitrary custom prefixes without manual static route management.

recent_posts.title: Adding machinectl support to microvm.nix
recent_posts.summary: A developer added machinectl integration and SSH-over-VSOCK support to microvm.nix, enabling NixOS VMs to appear natively in systemd's machine management tooling. The implementation leverages systemd 259's new RegisterMachineEx() API to register rich VM metadata (VSockCID, SSHAddress, NetworkInterfaces, etc.) while falling back to older APIs on earlier hosts. A new guest option enables sshd over VSOCK, and a microvm -s helper handles host-side SSH connections. The work also includes regression tests for machined registration, argument splitting, and edge cases in the imperative service template. The PR was submitted upstream as microvm.nix PR #453.

recent_posts.title: Traffic Shaping with CAKE on NixOS
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to eliminating bufferbloat on a 1 Gbit fiber connection using CAKE (Common Applications Kept Enhanced) SQM on NixOS. Covers how CAKE works — including AQM, flow isolation, Deficit Round Robin, and overhead compensation — and compares it to alternatives like fq_codel and HTB. Includes a complete NixOS systemd service configuration with egress shaping directly on the PPPoE interface and ingress shaping via an IFB virtual interface, with detailed explanations of key parameters like bandwidth headroom, overhead values, and the wash option.

recent_posts.title: Running a RIPE Atlas Probe on NixOS with Starla
recent_posts.summary: A RIPE Atlas v2 hardware probe reached end-of-life, prompting a switch to Starla — an unofficial Rust reimplementation of the RIPE Atlas software probe. Starla ships a NixOS module with hardened systemd configuration, CAP_NET_RAW for raw sockets, and a built-in Prometheus exporter. Setup involves adding the flake's nixosModules.default, generating an Ed25519 SSH key on first boot, and registering the public key with RIPE. The probe runs entirely outbound via SSH tunnels to RIPE controllers on port 443, supports all measurement types (ping, traceroute, DNS, HTTP, TLS, NTP), and consumes negligible resources (~5 MB RSS). Key caveats include Starla being unofficial and the importance of backing up the probe's SSH key to preserve credit history.
